title: How to Prepare for Newborn Photos: An RGV Parent Checklist
description: How to prepare for newborn photos in the RGV, step by step: when to book, the day before, the morning of, what to bring and what happens at the session.
focus: how to prepare for newborn photos
h1: How to prepare for newborn photos: a step-by-step checklist
dek: From the day you book to the day your images arrive, here’s what to do at each stage — and the things you can stop worrying about.
intro:
To prepare for newborn photos, reserve your date in the second or third trimester, send us a message when baby arrives, and plan a full feeding, easy-off clothes and a warm, cozy car ride for session day. All you need to bring is your baby, feeding supplies, a pacifier if your baby uses one, and extra diapers — we take care of everything else.

Below is the full checklist for Rio Grande Valley families, one step at a time. It runs from pregnancy all the way to the day your edited images arrive.

sections.h2: Step 1: Book in your second or third trimester
sections.html:
Preparing for newborn photos starts before baby is born. Get in touch in the second or third trimester, and a spot is saved for you around your due date. The reasons behind that timing are in our post on when to do newborn photos.

  • Choose your session. Sunshine is baby only; Wonderland adds siblings and parents.
  • Planning maternity portraits too? That’s the perfect moment to reserve the newborn session at the same time.
  • Send your request. Use the online booking form or call or text (409) 354-3075. We reply within 24 hours.
  • Reserve your date. A 50% deposit via Zelle saves your spot, and the balance is due on session day.
  • Save our number. Add it to your phone now, so it’s easy to find in the blur after delivery.

sections.h2: Step 2: Send a message when baby arrives
sections.html:
Once baby is here, send us a quick message. We’ll pick a day for your session between day 5 and day 14, Monday through Saturday by appointment. If baby comes early or late, nothing changes on your end — the date simply follows baby’s arrival.

This is an easy job to hand off. A partner, grandparent or friend can send the text while you rest, and you can join the conversation whenever you have a free hand. Keep it simple: baby is here, and you’re ready to pick a day.

If you’ve booked Wonderland, it’s also a good time to settle on family outfits. Our guide on what to wear for newborn photos has ideas for parents and siblings.

sections.h2: Step 3: Pack a very short bag
sections.html:
Here’s the complete list of what to bring. It’s short on purpose:

  • Your baby
  • Feeding supplies — whatever you’d normally pack for a few hours out
  • A pacifier, if your baby uses one
  • Extra diapers

We take care of everything else. Wraps, outfits, bonnets, headbands, little beds, baskets and backdrops are ready before you walk in, so there’s no need to buy props or pack a bag of outfits for baby. If you’re booking Wonderland, the only extra planning is what the family will wear.

sections.h2: Step 4: Get ready the day before
sections.html:
A little prep the day before keeps the morning calm. Here’s what to do:

  • Set the bag by the door. Check it against the list above, then leave it where you can’t miss it.
  • Lay out baby’s clothes. Choose something that opens at the front, like a zip-up or snap sleeper.
  • Hang up family outfits. For Wonderland, keep everyone’s clothes together so nothing gets missed in the rush.
  • Save the location. Once we’ve shared the exact session location after booking, add it to your maps app so you’re not searching for it on the day.
  • Charge your phone. You’ll want it for directions, and for a quick text to us if you’re running behind.
  • Plan your departure. Work backward from your session time, leaving room for a feeding and a few spare minutes.

Then rest as much as a newborn allows. Nothing else needs to be bought, borrowed or ironed for baby.

sections.h2: Step 5: The morning of your session
sections.html:
A calm morning helps baby arrive sleepy and settled. Three things matter most:

  • A feeding plan. Many families time a full feeding shortly before they leave, so baby starts the ride content. On a longer drive, you can also plan to feed when you arrive — there’s always time to pause. If you bottle-feed, pack one more bottle than you think you’ll need.
  • Easy-off clothes. Dress baby in that front-opening outfit, and skip anything snug, layered or fussy.
  • A warm car ride. Babies tend to stay drowsy when they’re cozy. On a cool morning, warm the car up before you buckle baby in; in a hot Valley summer, run the A/C for a few minutes first so the car is comfortable, not hot.

Have breakfast and something to drink before you go, too. The session runs about 2–3 hours, and you’ll enjoy it more if you’re not running on empty.

Driving in from farther away?

If you’re coming from the other end of the Valley, give yourself a little extra cushion. From Weslaco it’s about 20–25 minutes and from Mercedes about 25–30 minutes, while San Benito is about 40–50 minutes and Los Fresnos about 55–65 minutes. Leave 15 minutes earlier than you think you need, so a diaper change or feeding stop doesn’t make you late.

sections.h2: Step 6: What happens during the 2–3 hour session
sections.html:
The studio is warm, quiet and clean, and everything is set up before you arrive. Adrisabel photographs every session herself — she’s trained in safe newborn posing, with 15+ years of experience and hundreds of babies photographed. You can read more about Adrisabel before your day.

Your baby sets the pace. We pause for feeding, cuddles, soothing and diaper changes whenever baby needs them, which is why newborn sessions take about 2–3 hours. Every pose is gently supported, and a parent is always close by. If baby wakes, fusses or needs a feed partway through, that’s built into the plan, not a problem.

In a Wonderland session, siblings and parents join in for family portraits too. Either way, your main job is to rest, feed and cuddle when needed, and watch your baby’s first portraits take shape.

sections.h2: Step 7: Choose your favorites at the end
sections.html:
When the session wraps up, we sit together and help you choose your favorite images. There’s no proof gallery to sort through at home later — one less task during those busy newborn weeks.

Every image is hand-selected, curated and edited, and your edited images are delivered within one week. The balance is due on session day, so it’s all settled before you head home.

A little thought ahead of time makes choosing easier. Talk with your partner about where the photos will live — a nursery wall, an album, a birth announcement — and any moments you’d love to have. For anything else, our frequently asked questions page has more answers.

faq.q: Can siblings be in the newborn photos?
faq.a: Yes — Wonderland is the session for that, with baby, big brothers or sisters and parents all in the photos. Sunshine photos are of baby only.

faq.q: Can we add more photos than our package includes?
faq.a: Yes. Extra edited photos can be added to any session, which helps if you fall in love with more images than you expected while choosing favorites.

faq.q: Can I bring something of our own for the photos?
faq.a: Of course — a meaningful item from home is always welcome, like a hand-knit hat or a keepsake passed down in your family. The studio already has wraps, outfits and props ready, so it’s completely optional.
